newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa, Zimbabwe in fresh talks on trade deal.
newsitem.headline: South Africa, Zimbabwe in fresh talks on trade deal.

text.p: South Africa and Zimbabwe held talks this week on details of an agreement aimed at ending a four-year trade dispute, Pretoria's foreign affairs department said on Thursday.
The two countries reached agreement in principle in August, when President Nelson Mandela's government agreed to cut some tariffs on Zimbabwean goods, particularly textiles.
The department of foreign affairs said in a statement that a joint technical working group met in Harare on Wednesday to thrash out further details.

"Discussions focused on the proposals...by Zimbabwe for improved market access for its exports to South Africa," the statement said, adding that the two sides would meet again in January where Pretoria would present its response.

Zimbabwe says some of its industries were nearly crippled when Pretoria tripled import duties on textiles and manufactured goods in 1992, after the expiry of a 1964 preferential trade pact signed by then white-ruled Rhodesia and South Africa's former white government.
Harare considered the duties -- pegged at 90 percent -- to be punitive.
Wednesday's talks included discussions on products covered in the 1964 treaty as well as pharmaceuticals, chemicals, plastics, footwear, consumer electronics and ceramics.
